initials: A library module with a public function that returns the initials of a full name, upper-cased and separated by nothing: "ada marie lovelace" gives "AML". Blank or extra spaces are ignored. Include example lines.
low_stock_report: A command-line program that reads a JSON file of products (name, stock, reorder_level) whose path is the first argument, and prints one line per product whose stock is below its reorder level, lowest stock first.
letter_grades: A library module that turns a list of scores (0 to 100) into letter grades A to F using the usual 90/80/70/60 cut-offs, plus a function that counts how many students got each grade.
password_strength: A library module with a sum type Weak, Fair or Strong and a function that classifies a password: Strong needs at least 12 characters with letters, digits and another kind of character; Fair needs at least 8 characters; everything else is Weak. Include example lines.
title_length_tool: An agent tool, exposed to agents, that downloads a web page and returns the number of characters in its <title> element, failing with a clear error when the page has no title.
roman_numerals: A library module that converts an Integer from 1 to 3999 to a Roman numeral and a Roman numeral back to an Integer, failing with a typed error for invalid input. Include example lines for both directions.
compound_interest: A command-line program that prints a yearly schedule of a savings balance with compound interest, exact to the cent: starting amount, yearly rate in percent and number of years come from the command line.
fizz_words: A command-line program that prints the numbers from 1 to 100, replacing multiples of 3 with Fizz, multiples of 5 with Buzz, and multiples of both with FizzBuzz, using a pure function with example lines for the word choice.
request_window: A library module with a function that takes a sorted list of request times in seconds and a window length, and returns how many requests would be rejected if at most 10 requests are allowed in any window.
merge_sorted: A library module with a function that merges two sorted lists of Integers into one sorted list without duplicates, with example lines, and a test block for two empty lists.
